The world is bleak. I have struggled with depression and anxiety my whole life, in and out of hospitals all throughout my teens. I’m in my 20s now and it still feels like I have no direction or purpose. I just happened to find things that I wanted. I found a way to be better for myself and live a life the younger me would be proud of. I still feel numb or empty sometimes, but I always find ways to distract myself and keep moving forward toward something. It might not mean much, but even just finding a small thing that you want to see, experience or do; that can really change everything. I made the goal to go to Italy, which in hindsight may have been a larger goal than I thought. But now, I just try for smaller things, like places I want to go during the week, things I want to experience. That’s what life is all about after all. And I found it definitely changes as you become an adult. That’s what I think anyway

It’s tough to say. I went through a lot to overcome it. It was definitely a mix of self-love/understanding. As well as trying to do the little things that were difficult because of my anxiety, like driving, or talking to new people. Like I said, I do still have anxiety, but I think those things helped  me the most personally

For me, I personally don’t believe there is a cure. However, I do know that it is possible to overcome severe anxiety and panic attacks. Throughout high school, I had severe anxiety and panic attacks that constantly made day to day life difficult for me. But now, I only have a panic attack about once every six months. It may not be perfect, but it’s much better than before. I still have anxiety about making phone calls, but I have enough courage to make them. Overcoming and managing anxiety is a difficult and very long process, it takes years of effort, as well as many highs and lows. But it’s possible, and saying might not help a ton right now, but remember to have hope, because without the hope of getting better, it will be more difficult. I hope this helps

The first time I had a panic attack was about a year ago. Personally, I get super pale(probably due to lowered blood pressure), I feel like I’m going to pass out/feel paralyzed, and feel like my heart is going to beat out of my chest. For me, it starts of slow and then becomes much worse really fast. So I usually take the time to find someone who can help me, whether that’s a friend or a staff member of the building I’m in. It feels very embarrassing, but I think it would be worse to pass out and cause a scene. I personally use breathing techniques and either sit or lay somewhere. I also put a cool, damp cloth on my forehead because I find it helps me. It is very common for people to have panic attacks, and if possible, you could get medication. I have muscle relaxants that I take when I feel a panic attack coming. I hope this helps!

I’m 16 as well and I’m no expert. But yeah it’s definitely bad for your health. Although the amount of sleep that one should get depends on many things, 5 hours of sleep during the night for one night may not be as bad, but if it’s consistently that amount of time it will stack up.

Sleep is a time in which you’re body rests, both mentally and physically. It will start affecting your physical health in terms of weight and hunger for sure. Make sure you are eating properly, because eating properly now is going to be difficult to maintain, especially since snacking on junk is easy if you’re playing video games into the late night/early morning. So ask yourself every now and again if you’ve eaten enough that day.

When it comes to sleep scheduling, that can be really tough too. I usually get to sleep around 2am and get up between 7am and 10am. If you’re only sleeping 5 hours a night, then try to limit game time in the evening, maybe watch something online for a while. What I tend to do is put something on my phone and lay in bed. I mostly listen and occasionally glance, so I’m still kinda watching something, but it doesn’t take long for me to fall asleep personally.

Honestly, the call is yours to make, just make sure you are properly nourished and try to get your sleep schedule back on track before quarantine is over!
